data.title: Earnings week ahead: Banks were upbeat on the economy, now onto tech
data.description:
The big banks set the tone this week: consumers are still spending, businesses are borrowing again, and credit isn’t getting worse. That’s good for growth, but it isn’t the demand destruction the Fed may need. September CPI came in at 3.7% headline and 2.6% core, both above forecast, and futures now price October no-change at 73%. The FOMC meets October 27–28, so next week’s earnings are the last real-economy check before the decision.

Monday, Oct 19

data.title: Bitcoin is little changed on the day, and pushing against a key crossroad.  What next?
data.description: Bitcoin has spent the early part of the week moving back and forth across its 100- and 200-hour moving averages (they are near converged near $82,500). Each break has offered an opportunity for the buyers  to take control. However, sellers prevailed.  The price moved away from those moving averages and low but similarly, sellers reached support and found that momentum faded as well. The price pushed higher.

data.title: AvaTrade Accelerates Global Growth with Acquisition of Forex Pioneer FXCM
data.description:
Agreement with Jefferies’ Stratos Group brings a 25-year Forex pioneer into AvaTrade’s multi-asset ecosystem and opens AvaTrade’s AI-powered platforms to FXCM clients worldwide.

AvaTrade, a leading global online trading broker, today announced a definitive agreement to acquire the FXCM business from Stratos Group International, LLC, a subsidiary of Jefferies Financial Group Inc. (NYSE: JEF). Under the agreement, AvaTrade Markets Ltd. will acquire substantially all of Stratos’ assets and business operations, which are expected to move to AvaTrade over approximately 120 days.

data.title: Morning Kickstart: Dollar falls despite hot inflation. USDJPY slips below key moving averages
data.description:
The US dollar continues its move to the downside today despite the hotter US CPI and PPI reports this week. Treasury yields are also higher this morning, but the greenback is struggling to attract buyers.

In the morning video above, I take a look at the three major currency pairs—EURUSD, USDJPY and GBPUSD—from a technical perspective. For each pair, I outline the bias, the risk-defining levels and the targets that would give either the buyers or sellers more control.

data.title: BOJ’s Ueda: We will continue to raise rates as underlying inflation approaches 2%
data.description:
• Want to gauge neutral rate estimate taking into account accumulative impact of past rate hikes on financial conditions, domestic prices
  • Hard to say anything clear about Japan’s neutral rate of interest
  • Takeaway from this week’s meetings was to exchange views with other policymakers on how Middle East conflict and AI demand could affect global, Japanese economies and inflation
  • As we have said, our policy has entered a new phase as underlying inflation is quite close to 2%, we cannot allow inflation to rise further
  • As underlying inflation is quite close to 2%, it is becoming more important than before to anchor inflation around our target
  • Haven’t been in touch with US Treasury Secretary Bessent since we met in Asheville
  • Timing, pace of future rate hikes will be decided looking at impact of FX, AI demand and Middle East developments on prices
  • We will discuss at upcoming meeting whether to tweak our assessment that underlying inflation is approaching 2%
  • Did not hear anything at this week’s meetings that deviated from our baseline view
  • Economic, price moves roughly in line with our forecasts
  • We will continue to raise interest rates as underlying inflation approaching 2%, financial conditions are accommodative
  • I felt that there were more policymakers at this meeting who were somewhat more bullish on AI demand than we had estimated
  • No big gap in view between what we have assessed on inflationary pressure from AI demand, and what I heard from global policymakers

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said at the IMF meetings that the BOJ will continue to raise interest rates, with underlying inflation approaching 2% and financial conditions still accommodative. The BOJ policy rate is currently at 1.25% and the market sees little chance of a hike at the October 30 meeting but that rises to 75% for the December 18 meeting.

data.title: Ethereum rebounds as dip-buyers pile in around key technical levels. Fundamental improvement or just a dead-cat bounce?
data.description:
Ethereum extended the losses yesterday following a hot US PPI report but eventually rebounded strongly as dip-buyers stepped in around key technical levels.

The macro and geopolitical pictures haven’t improved at all, so the rebound looks to be driven more by overstretched positioning.

data.title: Is EUR/USD finally turning the corner or is this just another false dawn?
data.description:
The past few weeks have been rather painful for EUR/USD buyers but it seems like things are finally taking a turn for the better. Ironically, this is all coming after hotter-than-expected US inflation data from the CPI and PPI reports this week. Yet, that is helping to give EUR/USD a lift as it pushes to 1.1260 today - the highest in a little over a week.

The immediate reaction to the US CPI report on Wednesday saw the pair fall to a low of 1.1114 before staging a meaningful rebound in the past few sessions. And with that, the technical picture is also starting to look more encouraging for buyers.

data.title: Crude oil remains supported amid Saudi-Houthi conflict and stalled US-Iran negotiations. What's next?
data.description:
Crude oil extended the gains yesterday into new highs as the lack of positive developments in the Middle East continues to support oil prices. The US-Iran negotiations have stalled over the conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

The US insists that Iran needs to address the nuclear programme first, while Tehran continues to prioritise its conditions, which include the lifting of the US blockade.

data.title: Solana's fundamentals are clouded by negative macro and geopolitical conditions. What's next?
data.description:
Solana has been under pressure in the past couple of weeks alongside the broader crypto market as deteriorating macro conditions and rising oil prices weighed on risk sentiment.

On the fundamental side, the upcoming Alpenglow upgrade could be a key catalyst. Scheduled for October 21, the consensus upgrade aims to reduce transaction finality, improving Solana's performance for applications requiring faster settlement.

data.title: Chart of the day: 10-year Treasury yields hit reverse this week but the real test is still ahead
data.description:
Seeing as to how the bond market is faring to end the week, you probably wouldn't have guessed that we actually got hotter-than-expected inflation data from both the US CPI and PPI reports in the past few days. In fact, you might even think it was the opposite. Yet, here we are.

10-year Treasury yields are down to 5.09%, poised for back-to-back weekly declines for the first time since June. That is certainly keeping things interesting with yields tumbling back to draw in the 5.00% mark again as broader market sentiment turns more cautious.

data.title: Gold shrugs off hot inflation data as market focus may be shifting to growth concerns
data.description:
Yesterday, US PPI came in much higher than expected, but gold's reaction was similar to what we saw after the US CPI release, that is the price initially spiked lower before recovering and rallying to new highs. Treasury yields also fell following the data, pointing to either overstretched positioning or growing concerns about the economic outlook.

Despite the Core PCE estimates now showing a monthly increase of 0.34% in October, the rate hike expectations for October actually fell after the PPI release. What’s more interesting is that further out the curve, we’ve seen a dovish repricing.

data.title: TMGM Named Official Financial Online Trading Sponsor of BIGBANG 2026–2027 WORLD TOUR <XX : COSMOS> in Sydney
data.description:
TMGM has been named the Official Financial Online Trading Sponsor of BIGBANG 2026–2027 WORLD TOUR <XX : COSMOS> in Sydney, bringing together the Sydney-founded global broker and one of Asia’s most recognised music acts as BIGBANG celebrates its 20th anniversary.

Taking place at Accor Stadium on 31 October 2026, the Sydney concert forms part of BIGBANG’s first world tour since 2017. The tour marks two decades since the group’s debut and its return to major international stages across Asia, North America, Europe and Oceania.
